  • [FEATURE] prometheus: Add WithUnit(unit string) option and explicit OpenMetrics unit support in CounterOpts, GaugeOpts, SummaryOpts, and HistogramOpts. #1392
  • [FEATURE] prometheus: Expose descriptor construction error through public Err() method on Desc. #1902
  • [FEATURE] promhttp: Add opt-in HandlerOpts.CoalesceGather to deduplicate concurrent Gather calls so overlapping scrapes share one collection cycle, preventing goroutine pile-up when the scrape rate outpaces collection time. #1969
  • [FEATURE] promhttp: HTTP handlers created by promhttp package now support metrics filtering by providing one or more name[] query parameters. The default behavior when none are provided remains the same, returning all metrics. #1925
  • [FEATURE] api/prometheus/v1: Add query formatting endpoint support (/format_query) and FormatQuery(ctx context.Context, query string) (string, error) method. #1846, #1856
  • [FEATURE] api/prometheus/v1: Add support for /status/tsdb/blocks endpoint via TSDBBlocks(ctx context.Context) ([]TSDBBlock, error) method. #1896
  • [FEATURE] exp/api/remote: Export BackoffConfig to allow customization when using WithAPIBackoff. #1895
  • [FEATURE] exp/api/remote: Add RetryCallBack to allow custom logging or handling on retry attempts in the remote write client. #1888, #1890
  • [ENHANCEMENT] prometheus/collectors/version: Allow specifying custom labels when registering the version collector. #1860
  • [ENHANCEMENT] api: Use cloned http.DefaultTransport when constructing default HTTP clients to prevent accidental mutations of shared global transport state. #1885
  • [BUGFIX] prometheus: Recover from collector panics during Gather() and return an error instead of crashing the process. #1961
  • [BUGFIX] prometheus: Fix cpu-seconds unit suffix handling for metric go_cpu_classes_gc_mark_assist_cpu_seconds. #1991
  • [BUGFIX] promhttp: InstrumentHandlerDuration and InstrumentHandlerCounter no longer panic when given an observer/counter that does not implement ExemplarObserver/ExemplarAdder (e.g. a SummaryVec). The exemplar is dropped and the value is recorded via the plain Observe/Add path, matching the safe-cast already used by Timer.ObserveDurationWithExemplar. #2005
  • [BUGFIX] api/prometheus/v1: Fall back to GET requests when POST requests return 403 Forbidden or method not allowed. #2030
  • [BUGFIX] api: Respect context cancellation inside httpClient.Do. #1971
  • [BUGFIX] exp/api/remote: Fix compression buffer pooling where compressed buffers were released prematurely, causing corrupted remote-write payloads. #1889
  • [BUGFIX] exp/api/remote: Reject malformed snappy payloads declaring huge decoded sizes. Enforce a 32MB decoded-size limit to prevent OOM from oversized remote-write requests. #1917
  • [BUGFIX] exp/api/remote: Ensure remote write v2 headers cannot be returned on v1 requests. #1927

title: fix: api.JobOutput decoding matches the Launcher wire protocol
description:
## Description

The launcher sends outputType in job output stream requests as an integer. The SDK previously implemented UnmarshalText, so encoding/json treated the field as a string. Every output request failed to decode, crashing the plugin read loop and triggering restarts.

JobOutput is a plain int, so encoding/json handles the integer form natively in both directions. Remove the custom text/JSON methods.

title: fix(cache): poll for goroutine exit in TestCloseStopsGoroutine
description:
## Summary

- `close(r.done)` signals `Close()` to unblock, but the goroutine may still be counted by `runtime.NumGoroutine()` for a brief window while the Go scheduler finalizes it
- Replaces the immediate snapshot with a polling loop (up to 100ms with `runtime.Gosched()` yields) so the test is robust on loaded CI runners
- Fixes the `TestCloseStopsGoroutine` failure on `main` introduced after PR #18 merged and was exposed by the Go 1.25 CI matrix on ubuntu-latest

## Test plan

- [ ] CI passes on both Go 1.25 and 1.26, ubuntu and macos

The Launcher uses this to surface a pre-fill hint for constraint inputs in Workbench — the Slurm plugin populates it from `launcher.slurm.conf` constraint definitions.
- Bumps `APIVersion` from `{3, 7, 0}` to `{3, 8, 0}`.

- `just build-examples` — clean

title: fix(cache): remove context from NewJobCache; Close() is sole lifecycle control
description:
Fixes #18.

## Problem

`NewJobCache` accepted a `context.Context`, implying the cache would react to cancellation. It did — partially. The background goroutine's shutdown path ended with `r.done <- struct{}{}` on an unbuffered channel that is only drained by `Close()`. Canceling the context without calling `Close()` left the goroutine blocked forever on that send. Our own `examples/inmemory` plugin triggered this, surviving only because the process exited immediately after.

## Solution

Remove the `context.Context` parameter. `Close()` is now the sole lifecycle control — it closes the update channel, the goroutine's `for range` loop exits, cleanup runs, and `Close()` drains `done`.

## Shutdown safety improvements (surfaced during review)

- **`done` channel buffered (cap 1)** — goroutine can always send without a receiver, preventing a deadlock if a panic fires before `Close()` is called
- **`sync.Once` in `Close()`** — idempotent; subsequent calls are no-ops
- **`atomic.Bool closed`** — set before `close(r.ch)` so `notify()` and subscribe methods detect shutdown without holding a lock
- **`notify()` TOCTOU guard** — checks `closed` then uses a targeted `recover()` for the narrow race window; re-panics for anything other than `"send on closed channel"`
- **Goroutine cleanup** — inner defer guarantees `r.done` is always sent even if cleanup panics; panic path skips `r.mu.Lock()` to avoid deadlock
- **`r.mu` during teardown** — subscriber map iteration in the cleanup defer now holds `r.mu`, preventing a race with concurrent subscribe calls
- **Late subscriber protection** — `subscribeToID`/`subscribeToUser` check `closed` under `r.mu` and close the caller's channel immediately rather than leaving it stranded
- **`subscriber.closed` flag** — prevents double-close when `Notify()` and `subManager.Close()` both try to close the same channel
- **Drop logging at `Warn`** — per-subscriber channel-full drops now log at `Warn` (consistent with the existing `Warn` in `notify()`)
- **Store error logged** — `Close()` logs the store error explicitly so it is durable even when the return value is discarded

## Other changes

- `examples/inmemory/main.go` now defers `Close()` (previously never closed the cache)
- Conformance test cleanups check the `Close()` error via `t.Errorf` instead of discarding it
- All signature references updated across docs, examples, and `plugintest`

## Tests (`cache/cache_test.go` — first unit tests for this package)

- `TestCloseStopsGoroutine` — regression for #18
- `TestDoubleCloseIsNoOp` — verifies `sync.Once` guard
- `TestNotifyCloseConcurrent` — exercises the `notify`/`Close` TOCTOU window under the race detector
- `TestSubscribeAfterClose` — verifies late subscribers get an immediate close signal
- `TestSubscriberCanceledContextCloseGuard` — verifies `sub.closed` prevents double-close

title: feat(logger): add logging.conf support via LogConfig and LoadLogConfig
description:
## Summary

Closes #33.

Adds `logging.conf` support to the Go SDK logger so plugins respect the same log-level and log-destination settings as every other Workbench component.

### New API

- **`LogConfig`** struct — holds resolved `Level`, `Type` (`file`|`stderr`), and `Dir`
- **`LoadLogConfig(executableName string, defaults LogConfig) (LogConfig, error)`** — reads `/etc/rstudio/logging.conf` (or `$RS_LOG_CONF_FILE`), applies `[*]` global and `[@executable]` per-binary sections, then applies env-var overrides (`RS_LOG_LEVEL`, `RS_LOGGER_TYPE`, `RS_LOG_DIR`). Env vars always win.
- **`NewLogger`** and **`MustNewLogger`** now accept `LogConfig` instead of `(debug bool, loggingDir string)`

Legacy CLI flags (`--enable-debug-logging`, `--logging-dir`) become the `defaults` argument to `LoadLogConfig`, so they continue to work when `logging.conf` is absent or silent on a setting.

### Correctness fixes included

- `WithAttrs`/`WithGroup`: three-index slice cap (`s[:len(s):len(s)]`) prevents backing-array aliasing between child handlers — required by the `slog.Handler` contract
- `applySection`: empty-value guard on `log-level` and `logger-type` keys (a blank `log-level =` now leaves the default unchanged rather than silently overriding to `LevelWarn`)
- `LoadLogConfig`: `os.Stat` check before `ini.LoadSources` — non-regular-file paths (directories, FIFOs, devices) return an explicit error rather than silently falling back to defaults
- `LoadLogConfig`: env overrides applied on all non-error return paths, including when no conf file is present
- `examples/inmemory`: clamp level to at least `DEBUG` after `LoadLogConfig` when `--enable-debug-logging` is set, preserving the flag's documented "enforces at least DEBUG" contract

## Test plan

- [ ] `go test ./...` — all packages pass
- [ ] `go test ./logger/... -race` — no races
- [ ] Verify `examples/inmemory` builds: `go build ./examples/inmemory`
- [ ] On a machine with `/etc/rstudio/logging.conf`: confirm plugin respects `log-level` setting
- [ ] Confirm `RS_LOG_LEVEL=debug` overrides conf-file level
- [ ] Confirm `--enable-debug-logging` is not lowered by a `log-level=warn` in conf

title: fix(launcher): use flag.Func for --enable-debug-logging to accept space-separated value
description:
## Summary

- Fixes #28
- The launcher always invokes plugins with `--enable-debug-logging 0` or `--enable-debug-logging 1` (space-separated, never `=`-joined). `flag.BoolVar` treats the value as an optional `=`-suffix, so `0`/`1` became stray positional args that halted `flag.Parse` — silently dropping `--scratch-path`, `--logging-dir`, `--plugin-name`, and every other subsequent flag.

title: fix(logger): render slog.Group attributes instead of dropping them
description:
## Summary

Closes #15. The Workbench-style slog handler in `logger/` silently dropped any attribute whose resolved value was a group — including `slog.Group(...)` and types whose `LogValue()` returned `slog.GroupValue(...)`. A secondary `fallthrough` bug also dropped non-error `slog.KindAny` values. Both were data-loss bugs with no error, warning, or hint to the caller.

- **Fix:** Replace the single-pass `formatAttr` with a recursive `appendAttr` walker plus a `formatValue` scalar helper. Group values flatten to dotted keys (`job.id: 42`), matching the prefix style `WithGroup` already produces — so callers get the same output whether they attach fields via `WithGroup(...)`, inline `slog.Group(...)`, or a `LogValuer` resolving to a group.
- **Contract compliance:** Empty-key groups inline their children, empty groups are omitted entirely, and zero `slog.Attr{}` values are skipped — all per the `slog.Handler` contract.
- **`KindAny` change:** Non-error `KindAny` values now render via `v.String()` (which is `fmt.Sprint(v.Any())`) instead of being silently dropped. Error-typed `KindAny` values continue to render via `err.Error()`.

## Test plan

- [x] `just check` passes (fmt, lint, full module tests)
- [x] `go test -race ./logger/...` passes
- [x] Verbatim test from #15 passes end-to-end through `NewLogger` and a real on-disk log file (`TestIssue15Reproducer`)
- [x] 15 test functions covering:
  - Scalars (7 subtests: bool true/false, string, int, float, duration, time)
  - Inline `slog.Group` flattening
  - `LogValuer` returning a group, and `LogValuer` returning a scalar
  - Nested groups (`a.b.c`)
  - Mixed scalar + sub-group in one group
  - `WithGroup` + inline-group composition
  - `WithAttrs` (pre-bound via `.With(...)`) + inline-group
  - Empty-key group inlining
  - Empty group omission (top-level and nested inside a non-empty group)
  - Group key containing a literal `.`
  - `KindAny` error and non-error

## Notes for reviewers

- The added explicit `case slog.KindGroup, slog.KindLogValuer:` arm in `formatValue` is defensive-only and unreachable in normal operation (see the comment); it exists to satisfy `exhaustive` linting under `default-signifies-exhaustive: false`.
- The `KindAny` non-error behavior change is a visible difference, but the prior behavior was silent data loss — no caller can be relying on the absence of output for a logged field.

title: Sync Go SDK with Plugin API v3.7.0 protocol fields
description:
## Summary

Audits the Go SDK against the canonical C++ Launcher and first-party plugin implementations to close gaps between the wire protocol and what the SDK exposed. All changes match observed C++ behavior.

- **Add `InitContainer` type and `Job.InitContainers`** — init containers run before the main job container when the cluster advertises `supportsInitContainers`. Includes `Job.InstanceID` (Launcher-assigned persistent identifier that plugins must round-trip unchanged), and `Mount.Name` (optional label for a file system mount).
- **Remove `MultiCluster` extension** — the `requestMultiClusterInfo`/`responseMultiClusterInfo` message types (wire value 17) were removed from the protocol. The request handler and response writer method have been deleted accordingly.
- **Add `memoryUsageBytes` to metrics** — `PluginMetrics.MemoryUsageBytes` and `MetricsResponse.memoryUsageBytes` were missing. The Launcher always reads this field; zero is treated as unknown rather than a measurement of zero bytes.
- **Fix `ResourceProfile` serialization** — `Queue` and `Constraints` were missing `omitempty`, causing them to always serialize even when empty. C++ only sends these fields conditionally.
- **Add `name` and `statusCode` to job status stream responses** — `WriteJobStatus` now accepts `name` and `statusCode`, matching `JobStatusStream::getJobStatusJson` in the C++ SDK. `statusCode` is forwarded from `Job.StatusCode` through the `statusUpdate` pub/sub path and omitted when empty; `name` is always sent (matching C++ behavior).

## Breaking changes

`launcher.StreamResponseWriter.WriteJobStatus` has a new signature:

```go
// Before
WriteJobStatus(id api.JobID, name, status, msg string) error

// After
WriteJobStatus(id api.JobID, name, status, statusCode, msg string) error
```

Plugins that implement `StreamResponseWriter` directly (rather than delegating to the cache helpers) must add the `statusCode` parameter. Pass an empty string if the scheduler does not use status codes.

## Test plan

- [ ] `go test ./...` passes
- [ ] `go test -race ./...` passes
- [ ] Verify `Job.InitContainers`, `Job.InstanceID`, and `Mount.Name` round-trip correctly through `Job.WithFields`
- [ ] Verify `memoryUsageBytes` appears in metrics JSON output with a non-zero value
- [ ] Verify `statusCode` is omitted from stream responses when empty, present when set

title: Add Plugin API v3.7.0 metrics support
description:
## Summary

- Add `MetricsPlugin` optional capability interface for plugins to report periodic metrics (uptime, cluster interaction latency) via unsolicited wire messages (type 203)
- Implement `Histogram` type with swap-on-drain pattern for thread-safe accumulation without requiring Prometheus reset
- Add metrics collection loop with panic recovery to isolate plugin metric failures from framework metrics
- Use non-blocking channel sends to prevent metrics goroutine from blocking the protocol handler
- Wire protocol emits non-cumulative per-bucket counts matching the C++ SDK format
- Add conformance test scenario `RunMetrics` for verifying plugin metrics compliance
- Bump API version to v3.7.0

## Design highlights

- **Push-based**: Plugin initiates unsolicited metrics messages on a configurable interval (requestId/responseId both zero)
- **Panic isolation**: Framework metrics (uptime) always report even if plugin's `CollectMetrics()` panics
- **Non-blocking sends**: `select/default` pattern on the metrics channel prevents goroutine deadlock
- **Bucket format**: Non-cumulative per-bucket counts on the wire, matching the C++ Launcher SDK

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests for `Histogram` (observe, drain, reset, concurrent access, invalid inputs, constructor validation)
- [x] Unit tests for `metricsLoop` (timing, response format, panic recovery)
- [x] Conformance scenario for metrics reporting

title: Add Plugin API v3.6.0 config reload support
description:
## Summary

Implements the Config Reload request/response pair from Plugin API v3.6.0 (Launcher v2.19.0), allowing the Launcher to request plugins to reload their configuration at runtime without restarting.

- Add `ConfigReloadablePlugin` optional interface — plugins implement `ReloadConfig(ctx context.Context) error` to handle reload requests
- Add `ConfigReloadError` type for classified reload failures (`Load`, `Validate`, `Save`) and `ConfigReloadErrorType` enum
- Plugins that don't implement `ConfigReloadablePlugin` automatically send a success response
- Wire protocol: message type 202, response includes `errorType` (int enum) and `errorMessage` (string)

## Changes

| Area | Files |
|------|-------|
| API types | `api/types.go`, `api/types_test.go` |
| Protocol | `internal/protocol/rpc.go`, `internal/protocol/stream.go`, `internal/protocol/rpc_test.go` |
| Plugin interface & handler | `launcher/launcher.go`, `launcher/launcher_test.go` |
| Test utilities | `plugintest/mocks.go` |
| Docs | `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/API.md`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `docs/GUIDE.md` |

## Design decisions

- **Optional interface pattern**: Follows existing `BootstrappedPlugin`, `MultiClusterPlugin`, and `LoadBalancedPlugin` patterns — type assertion in the handler dispatch
- **Error classification**: `ReloadConfig` returns `error`; plugins return `*ConfigReloadError` for classified errors (Load/Validate/Save) or plain `error` for unclassified failures (mapped to `ReloadErrorUnknown`)
- **`RequestFromJSON` export**: Renamed from `requestFromJSON` to enable handler dispatch tests without depending on internal struct construction

## Test plan

- [x] `just build-examples` — examples still build

- [x] Handler dispatch: not-implemented (auto-success), success, `ConfigReloadError`, plain error, wrapped `ConfigReloadError`
- [x] `ConfigReloadErrorType.String()` covers all enum values plus invalid input
